items.body_md:
On August 7–8, Skillz filed pro hac vice motions for Michael Ardeljan and Amy C. Quartarolo of Latham & Watkins (Dkts. 50–51), bringing Skillz's admitted Latham team in this proceeding to five attorneys following the Goldberg, Harris, and Schrock admissions entered August 6. Dkt. 52 is a notice of service. All are procedural and carry no independent weight on recovery or timing.

The substantive posture is unchanged from Saturday's edition. Judge Walrath's temporary injunction — staying collection and enforcement against Papaya's U.S. assets over Skillz's objection — remains the operative protection, as reported by __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__. The Latham buildout does, however, add color to the deposition notices (Dkts. 53–55) filed the same day: Skillz is assembling a full litigation team ahead of the September 3 recognition hearing, not merely preserving rights. The three noticed witnesses — Oriel Bachar, Pinni Yaniv, and James Kong — map directly to the center-of-main-interests question. Yaniv, identified by __[The Jerusalem Post](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-904473)__ as a Meitar Law Offices partner representing Papaya in the Israeli proceeding, is the architect of the Tel Aviv arrangement; his deposition, alongside Bachar's, signals Skillz intends to contest where Papaya actually manages its affairs, not merely argue the legal standard. The financial gap driving that contest has not changed: Judge Cote's disgorgement award stands at approximately $719 million plus approximately $10.1 million in fees and costs per __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__, against a supervised Israeli fund expected to hold approximately $100 million during 2026 per __[World Casino Directory](https://news.worldcasinodirectory.com/papaya-gaming-files-chapter-15-after-719m-verdict-123873)__.

The next hard milestones are the objection deadline of August 27 and the recognition hearing before Judge Walrath on September 3, 2026, at 9:30 AM (virtual). Whether deposition dates for Bachar, Yaniv, and Kong are scheduled and confirmed before August 27 will indicate whether Skillz is building a factual record for a contested COMI challenge at the hearing or using the notices as pre-hearing leverage.

items.body_md:
On August 7, the clerk docketed the notice scheduling the § 341 meeting of creditors (Dkt. 97), setting the first formal opportunity for the U.S. Trustee and creditors to examine the debtors under oath. The § 341 meeting is procedural but carries timing significance: its scheduling confirms the case is moving on the standard Chapter 11 administrative track in parallel with the sale process, and any creditor — including wallet holders — may appear and pose questions directly to the debtors' representatives. The specific date and location are not established from available docket text; confirmation requires the docket entry itself.

Dkts. 98–100 — the objection, accompanying document, and exhibit filed on August 7 and 8 against the bidding procedures and sale motion — remain the substantive weight of the hearing set for Thursday, August 14 at 11 a.m. ET before Judge O'Hagan. The identity of the objecting party and the specific grounds are not established from available docket text. Thor CALAP LLC's no-cause diligence termination right expired by its contractual terms on August 9; no termination notice has appeared on the docket and no press outlet has reported exercise of that right, which is consistent with both the $15 million Pyote and $37 million Tarbush agreements remaining operative — but the debtors have not affirmatively represented that status on the record. A termination delivered directly to the debtors need not surface immediately as a court filing, so the stalking-horse status remains unverified until the August 14 hearing or an earlier affirmative representation by counsel.

The Notice of Docketing Error (filed August 7, no docket number assigned) is ministerial and carries no bearing on the substantive record. The next concrete milestone is the August 14 hearing at 11 a.m. ET: Judge O'Hagan's ruling on the bidding procedures and sale motion — including resolution of the Dkt. 98 objection — will determine whether the September 8 qualified-bid deadline, the September 10 auction, and the proposed September 16 sale hearing hold. For the 11,700 wallet holders carrying $163,723,500 in unsecured IOU claims, Thursday's ruling is the first judicial read on whether the sale framework survives intact.

items.lede: On August 8, the BNC issued the certificate of mailing for the lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146, completing service and starting the response clock. No further substantive filings have landed on the docket since.
items.body_md:
On August 8, the BNC issued the certificate of mailing for the lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146, completing service and starting the response clock. No further substantive filings have landed on the docket since. Dkts. 147–155 and 158 — pro hac vice admissions, notices of appearance, affidavits in support of those admissions, and the BNC certificate itself — are entirely procedural and routine.

The lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146 remains the open substantive item. Its movant, the specific asset or claim at issue, and the precise relief sought are still unverified without a PACER pull. Under S.D. Tex. Bankruptcy Local Rule 4001-1, the response deadline runs 14 days from service — placing it on or about August 22, two days before the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24. That sequencing creates three possible paths into the August 24 docket: a fully contested hearing on the lift-stay motion if a response is timely filed; an agreed order resolving it before the hearing; or a deemed unopposed grant if no response appears. Each path carries different consequences for unsecured creditors. A contested or granted motion that reaches estate property — inventory, a receivable, a leased facility — removes that asset from the pool before any sale process has run. An agreed resolution, depending on its terms, may accomplish the same result under a consent order. Neither outcome can be sized without the document's contents, and that gap in the record remains the threshold analytical problem.

The next concrete milestone is the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24, 2026. That hearing is expected to carry the first-day-to-final conversions, the first formal appearance of the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors on the record, and — depending on whether a response to Dkt. 146 is filed by August 22 — the lift-stay motion itself.
